# Fix send-campaign-emails to accept frontend payload format

## Summary

Fixes the "Error sending campaign: Send failed:" error by aligning the `send-campaign-emails.mts` Netlify function with what the frontend actually sends.

**Root cause:** The frontend sends `{ campaign: {...}, recipients: [...], sendOption: "now" }` but the function expected `{ campaign_id: 9 }` and tried to fetch recipients from an `email_campaign_recipients` queue table that was never populated.

**Key changes:**
- Accept campaign object and recipients array directly from frontend
- Map frontend field names (`fromName`, `fromEmail`, `htmlContent`) to internal format (`from_name`, `from_email`, `html_content`)
- Fix XANO API group from `api:PpStJiYV` to `api:iZd1_fI5` (EmailMarketing group)
- Generate tracking tokens from `email + campaign_id` instead of expecting pre-generated tokens
- Send individual emails for proper per-recipient personalization
- Maintain backward compatibility with legacy `campaign_id` format

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Test sending a campaign end-to-end** - Send a test email from the deploy preview to verify emails actually arrive. I could not test this myself.
- [ ] **Verify XANO API group** - Confirm `api:iZd1_fI5` is the correct EmailMarketing API group in your XANO instance
- [ ] **Check tracking/analytics** - The tracking token generation changed from database-stored tokens to `base64(email:campaign_id)`. Verify open/click tracking still works if you rely on it.
- [ ] **Test with multiple recipients** - The function now sends individual emails per recipient instead of batching. Test with a small group (5-10) to verify all receive the email.

**Recommended test plan:**
1. Go to deploy preview URL
2. Create or select an existing campaign
3. Select a test subscriber list with 2-3 test emails you control
4. Send the campaign
5. Verify all test emails receive the message with correct formatting

### Notes

The `email_campaign_recipients` queue table was part of a planned architecture that was never implemented - no frontend code populates it. This PR bypasses that table entirely and uses the recipients provided directly by the frontend.

The main purpose of this PR is to allow empty splits when using split mode "graph". If, for instance, one has 4 GPUs, and this leads to a bad performance with split mode "graph", one could try using
```
-sm graph -ts 100,100,0,0 -ot "...=GPU2,...=GPU3"
```
to put all attention tensors, shared experts tensors, and KV cache on GPU 0 and 1, and then use GPU 2 and 3 to offload MoE tensors. In that case tensor parallel (and corresponding synchronization plus data exchange overhead) for attention and shared experts is done on only 2 GPUs, hopefully resulting in a better performance.

author: hasb4k
body:
## Purpose
We encountered a "bug" with P/D disaggregation in our pre-prod env a while ago. Here is what we think happened:

Some requests were canceled on Prefill by our router/proxy because of a Timeout (let's say 20s here). Usually a Timeout usually stop/abort a request entirely (which is what we want). But with P/D disagg, you can be unlucky, if you have a lot of requests that will take 20s to prefill if at the same time:

- At the same time:
  - The requests finish the Prefill in 20s
  - The request timeout after 20s! And you trigger an abort
- But (on main) the request is unfree-able because the NIXL KVConnector considers [that requests with FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED should be delayed](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5aa9b090407d5fb9b89c05d28fab808623e3070c/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl_connector.py#L635) (which is what we want in most cases, but not when we abort a request)
- => this request is now in an un-freeable state for 5 minutes (ie. the default [VLLM_NIXL_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/1bb17ecb396f911beaa26ab0d3926d46154c7155/vllm/envs.py#L1374))
- The requests will be retried on another instance, and create the same issues
- If you are unlucky with a lot of requests similar, you exhaust the available KV Cache, and you start rejecting requests which creates a denial of service for a time :confused: 


This patch, force the removal of a delayed request when an abort happen

(cc @NickLucche)

# feat/14-matched-subsampling

This PR introduces the new script `matched_subsampling.py`, which identifies and returns the largest possible subset of samples from a merged compendium such that each metadata feature has equal representation across all compendia.

Example configs for this script are stored in `configs/matched_subsampling`.

`configs/matched_subsampling/polyA_vs_riboD_v25-01/disease.json`:
```json
{
    "out_dir_name": "polyA_riboD_disease_matched",
    "metadata_label": "disease",
    "compendia_set": [
        "Tumor_Compendium_25.01_PolyA_01_2025",
        "Tumor_Compendium_25.01_RiboD_01_2025"
    ]
}
```

The script outputs a `.tsv` file containing the Treehouse Sample IDs that constitute the matched subset of the full compendium. When compendia must be sampled down, the correct number of samples is selected at random. This output format matches the expected `sample_subset` input for the `process_data.py` config.

Read more about the script in `README.md`.

## Testing
Testing for the primary algorithm in `matched_subsampling.py` can be found in `tests/test_matched_subsampling.py`.

## Fix
Corrected the Treehouse Sample ID column header from `sample` to `th_dataset_id` in the pilot data to match the format used in the Treehouse Compendia.
